title: Ban Zhao Finishes Her Brother's History
text:
Ban Biao, a scholar of the first century AD, began writing a continuation of Sima Qian's great history of China. When he died, his son Ban Gu took over and reshaped the work into a history of the Former Han dynasty, the Book of Han. Ban Gu's twin brother, Ban Chao, became a famous general in Central Asia. Their younger sister, Ban Zhao, was married at fourteen, widowed young, and devoted herself to study.

In 92 AD Ban Gu was caught up in the fall of a powerful patron, the general Dou Xian. He was imprisoned and died there, leaving the Book of Han unfinished. According to her biography in the History of the Later Han, the emperor ordered Ban Zhao to complete it, giving her access to the imperial library. She finished the eight tables and, with the help of the scholar Ma Xu, the treatise on astronomy.

The book was so difficult that many readers could not follow it. The scholar Ma Rong, later one of the most famous classicists of the age, was sent to study it under her. Ban Zhao also served as teacher to the empress and the palace ladies, and wrote Lessons for Women, advice to her daughters. When she died, the empress dowager wore mourning for her.

The Book of Han, the work of a father, a son and a daughter, became the model for all later Chinese dynastic histories.
lesson: Family work can pass from one generation to the next, and to whoever is most able to carry it. Talent in a family should not be overlooked because of who holds it.
people: Ban Zhao, Ban Gu, Ban Biao, Ban Chao
source: Fan Ye, Hou Hanshu (History of the Later Han), biography of the wife of Cao Shishu (Ban Zhao)
